extracted.intended_audience: users of the fpadim.lib Letterplace library (computer-algebra / non-commutative Gröbner basis practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for fpadim.lib procedures that operate on Letterplace rings: computing mistletoes, K-dimension, Hilbert series, and converting between intvec/intmat representations and Letterplace monomials/polys. Includes usage, return values, assumptions, and notes for each procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: ivMis2Dim
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ivMis2Dim(M); M a list of intvecs. Return: int, the K-dimension of the given algebra. Purpose: Computing the K-dimension out of given mistletoes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mistletoes have to be ordered lexicographically -> OrdMisLex. Otherwise the returned value may differ from the K-dimension. basering must be a Letterplace ring. (Example shows setring R; intvec inputs; returns integer dimension.)

rubrics_metrics.name: ivOrdMisLex
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ivOrdMisLex(M); M a list of intvecs. Return: list, containing the ordered intvecs of M. Purpose: Orders a given set of mistletoes lexicographically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring and intvecs correspond to monomials. This is preprocessing; not needed if mistletoes are returned from the sickle algorithm. Each entry of the returned list is an intvec.

rubrics_metrics.name: ivSickle
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ivSickle(L,n,[degbound]); L a list of intmats, n an int, degbound an optional integer. Return: list, containing intvecs, the mistletoes of A/<L>. Purpose: Computing the mistletoes for a given Groebner basis L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring and all rows of each intmat correspond to a Letterplace monomial. If degbound is specified it must satisfy degbound <= attrib(basering,uptodeg). By default there is no degree bound. n is the number of variables. If the K-dimension is known to be infinite, a degree bound is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: ivSickleHil
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ivSickleHil(L,n[,degbound]); L a list of intmats, n an integer, degbound an optional integer. Return: list. Purpose: Computing the mistletoes and the Hilbert series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring and all rows of each intmat correspond to a Letterplace monomial. If degbound specified then degbound <= attrib(basering,uptodeg). If L is the list returned, then L[1] is an intvec (Hilbert series coefficients) and L[2] is a list containing the mistletoes as intvecs. I[k] is the (k-1)-th coefficient of the Hilbert series. If K-dimension is infinite a degree bound is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: ivSickleDim
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ivSickleDim(L,n[,degbound]); L a list of intmats, n an integer, degbound optional. Return: list. Purpose: Computing mistletoes and the K-dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring and all rows of each intmat correspond to a Letterplace monomial. If degbound specified degbound <= attrib(basering,uptodeg). If L is the list returned, then L[1] is an integer (K-dimension) and L[2] is a list containing the mistletoes as intvecs. n is number of variables. If K-dimension is infinite a degree bound is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpOrdMisLex
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: lpOrdMisLex(M); M an ideal of mistletoes. Return: ideal, containing the mistletoes, ordered lexicographically. Purpose: A given set of mistletoes is ordered lexicographically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring. This is preprocessing and not needed if mistletoes were returned from the sickle algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpSickle
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: lpSickle(G[,degbound,n]); G an ideal, degbound and n optional integers. Return: ideal. Purpose: Computing the mistletoes of K[X]/<G>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring. If degbound specified then degbound <= attrib(basering,uptodeg). If degbound is set, a degree bound will be added; 0 means no degree bound. Default: attrib(basering,uptodeg). n is number of variables; default attrib(basering,lV). If K-dimension is known to be infinite, a degree bound is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpSickleHil
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: lpSickleHil(G); Return: list. Purpose: Computing the Hilbert series and the mistletoes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring. If L is the list returned, then L[1] is an intvec corresponding to the Hilbert series, L[2] is an ideal, the mistletoes. degbound semantics: 0 means no degree bound; default attrib(basering,uptodeg). n default attrib(basering,lV). If I = L[1] then I[k] is (k-1)-th coefficient of Hilbert series. If K-dimension infinite, degree bound needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpSickleDim
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: lpSickleDim(G[,degbound,n]); G an ideal, degbound and n optional integers. Return: list. Purpose: Computing the K-dimension and the mistletoes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring. If L is the list returned, then L[1] is an integer (K-dimension) and L[2] is an ideal (mistletoes). degbound semantics as in lpSickle: 0 means no degree bound; default attrib(basering,uptodeg). n default attrib(basering,lV). If K-dimension infinite, degree bound needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: sickle
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sickle(G[,m, d, h, degbound]); G an ideal; m,d,h,degbound optional integers. Return: list. Purpose: Allowing the user to access all procs with one command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring. degbound semantics: if specified degbound <= attrib(basering,uptodeg). The returned object is always a list but entries may vary depending on flags. Case mapping: m=1,d=1,h=1 -> lpDHilbertSickle; m=1,d=1,h=0 -> lpSickleDim; m=1,d=0,h=1 -> lpSickleHil; m=1,d=0,h=0 -> lpSickle (default); m=0,d=1,h=1 -> lpDHilbert; m=0,d=1,h=0 -> lpKDim; m=0,d=0,h=1 -> lpHilbert; m=0,d=0,h=0 -> returns an error. If K-dimension is infinite a degree bound is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: ivMaxIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage example: ivMaxIdeal(l, lonly); l an integer, lonly an integer. RETURN: list. PURPOSE: computes a list of free monomials in intvec presentation with length <= l; if donly <> 0, only monomials of degree d are returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring. Note: see also lpMaxIdeal(). Examples show various l and lonly parameters and the returned intvec lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: lpMaxIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: lpMaxIdeal(d, donly); d an integer, donly an integer. RETURN: ideal. PURPOSE: computes a list of free monomials of degree at most d; if donly <> 0, only monomials of degree d are returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring and d <= attrib(basering,uptodeg). NOTE: analogous to maxideal(d) in the commutative case. Examples show returned ideals of monomials for various d and donly values.

rubrics_metrics.name: monomialBasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: monomialBasis(d, donly, J); d, donly integers, J an ideal. RETURN: ideal. PURPOSE: computes a list of free monomials in a Letterplace basering R of degree at most d and not contained in <LM(J)>; if donly <> 0, only monomials of degree d are returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a Letterplace ring, d <= attrib(basering,uptodeg), and J is a Groebner basis. Examples show monomial lists for various d and J; output excludes monomials in the leading monomial ideal of J.

rubrics_metrics.name: ivL2lpI
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ivL2lpI(L); L a list of intvecs. Return: ideal. Purpose: Transforming a list of intvecs into an ideal of Letterplace monomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume intvec corresponds to a Letterplace monomial and basering has to be a Letterplace ring. Note: assumptions will not be checked. Example shows intvecs u,v,w -> corresponding ideal monomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: iv2lp
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: iv2lp(I); I an intvec. Return: poly. Purpose: Transforming an intvec into the corresponding Letterplace polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume intvec corresponds to a Letterplace monomial and basering has to be a Letterplace ring. Note: assumptions will not be checked. Examples: iv2lp(u) -> x(1)*x(2)*y(3), etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: iv2lpList
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: iv2lpList(L); L a list of intmats. Return: ideal. Purpose: Converting a list of intmats into an ideal of corresponding monomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume the rows of each intmat in L correspond to a Letterplace monomial and basering has to be a Letterplace ring. Example shows lists of intmats producing an ideal of monomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: iv2lpMat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: iv2lpMat(M); M an intmat. Return: ideal. Purpose: Converting an intmat into an ideal of the corresponding monomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume the rows of M must correspond to Letterplace monomials and basering has to be a Letterplace ring. Examples demonstrate returning monomials contained in various intmats.

rubrics_metrics.name: lp2iv
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: lp2iv(p); p a poly. Return: intvec. Purpose: Transforming a monomial into the corresponding intvec.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering has to be a Letterplace ring. Note: assumptions will not be checked. Examples: lp2iv(x(1)*x(2)*z(3)) -> 1,1,3, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: lp2ivId
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: lp2ivId(G); G an ideal. Return: list. Purpose: Converting an ideal into a list of intmats, the corresponding intvecs forming the rows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering has to be a Letterplace ring. (Documented as a conversion utility; assumptions not checked.)
